comment: Copy to skills/<your-skill>/evals/evals.json -- the catalog contract, run
here on every pull request. Every routing prompt belongs in this file,
the `skill_should_trigger: false` near misses most of all: they assert
that nothing in the published bundle fires, which only this repo can
grade, and they are the cheapest cases in the suite.
Behavior cases are capped by time, not count: each skill's suite gets 15
minutes. Keep the ones that pin down what this skill exists to do, and
put the deep and slow ones in evals/extended_evals.json -- same shape,
same fields, run by the repo that owns this skill on its own CI. Moving a
case between the two files is a cut and paste.

evaluations.note: Tier 1. The same prompt grades routing AND what the agent then did.
evaluations.prompt: A task this skill should carry out end to end.
expected_behavior: A thing the agent must do, in plain language, graded by an LLM judge
unexpected_behavior: A mistake this skill exists to prevent

evaluations.prompt: Something a user would say that should make this skill fire.
A different phrasing of the same need, with none of the same keywords.

evaluations.note: Close to this skill's vocabulary but out of its scope: the wrong hardware, an adjacent domain, a question rather than a task.
evaluations.prompt: Something that sounds like this skill's territory but is not.
Another prompt that must not wake this skill up.
